subject: Migration: deployment mode selection (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — follow-up
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@luminalabs.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@luminalabs.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: deployment mode options after demo

Thanks for the demo today — it was really helpful. A few quick follow-ups from our side as we evaluate migration options from our current self-hosted stack:

- Clarify the trade-offs between Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private (VPC/on-prem) for: latency SLAs, cost predictability, and data residency.
- We currently route production traffic through an existing API gateway (internal) and have a legacy GPU cluster used for batch jobs. We also have an evaluation license with another LLM API provider that handles some traffic. Can Redwood support a phased migration where we use Hosted for burst/preview traffic while Dedicated backs steady production, and then move certain customers into Private VPC for HIPAA-regulated data?
- Security/compliance ask: we'll need evidence around isolation, KMS integration, and audit logs for the initial procurement review.

Next steps from our side: Elena and I want to align on a mutual action plan and get an initial cost/latency comparison for our 8k average tokens/day usage pattern (mostly chat with occasional long-context generation). Can you share a short recommendation and proposed next steps by EOD Friday PST?

Thanks,
Samir
Head of AI Platform, Lumina Labs
[Attachment: initial-architecture-snapshot.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 17:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode options after demo

Samir — really appreciate the clear asks and the architecture snapshot. High-level response below and we'll follow up with a short MAP (mutual action plan) and a cost/latency sketch by Friday.

High-level recommendations:
1) Hosted API (fastest path): good for pilot/beta and burst traffic. Minimal operational lift, predictable per-token pricing. Best if you need immediate scale and aren’t putting regulated data in the hosted plane.
2) Dedicated capacity: recommended if you want consistent throughput and predictable latency across peak windows. Reserved GPU pools mean lower per-token unit cost for steady traffic and easier SLOs.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem): necessary if you need network isolation, full control over keys (HSM/KMS), or on-prem requirements for compliance (e.g., HIPAA). Higher Ops and setup time but provides strict data residency and auditability.

Migration pattern we commonly see (and recommend for customers in similar setups):
- Phase 1: Pilot on Hosted for a subset of traffic + Continuous replication to Dedicated for baseline production.
- Phase 2: Move regulated customer traffic to Dedicated with VPC peering and optional Bring-Your-Own-Key.
- Phase 3: For the narrow set of customers needing on-prem, perform a Private deployment cutover while keeping hybrid fallback to Dedicated for burst capacity.

Security/compliance: we can provide SOC2 summary, audit log samples, and KMS integration docs. I'll attach a short deployment comparison and a migration checklist so your procurement can intake initial materials.

Next steps: I'll send a 1-page MAP + cost/latency sketch by Friday EOD PST and propose a 60-minute migration workshop next week to go over the checklist and the config choices. Does Tue/Thu next week work for you?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_deployment_comparison.pdf]
